content.stem: Kabir deposits a fixed sum every month in a recurring deposit account for \(2\tfrac{1}{2}\) years. The bank pays simple interest at 7.2% per annum, and the maturity value of the account is ₹39,348. Find the amount of his monthly instalment.

hints: Let the monthly instalment be ₹\(P\). How many instalments are paid in \(2\tfrac{1}{2}\) years?
Maturity value = total of the instalments + interest. Write both in terms of \(P\).

solution.modelAnswer: Let the instalment be ₹\(P\); \(n = 30\), \(r = 7.2\). Interest \(= P \times \tfrac{30 \times 31}{2 \times 12} \times \tfrac{7.2}{100} = 2.79P\). Maturity value \(= 30P + 2.79P = 32.79P = 39348\), so \(P = 1200\). The monthly instalment is ₹1,200.

steps.title: Set up
steps.explanation: Let the monthly instalment be ₹\(P\). There are 30 monthly instalments.

steps.title: Interest in terms of P
steps.explanation: Use the recurring deposit interest formula. The equivalent principal for one month is \(38.75P\).

steps.title: Maturity value
steps.explanation: Maturity value is the total amount deposited (\(30P\)) plus the interest.

steps.title: Solve
steps.explanation: The monthly instalment is ₹1,200. Check: deposits ₹36,000 + interest ₹3,348 = ₹39,348.

commonMistakes: Taking \(n = 2.5\) or \(n = 2\) instead of the number of months, 30.
Equating the interest alone (instead of the maturity value) to ₹39,348.
Forgetting to divide \(n(n+1)/2\) by 12 to convert month-rupees into a principal for one year.

alternativeMethods.title: Equivalent principal
alternativeMethods.description: The account is equivalent to a principal of \(P \times \tfrac{30 \times 31}{2} = 465P\) for one month, i.e. \(\tfrac{465P}{12}\) for one year. Simple interest \(= \tfrac{465P}{12} \times \tfrac{7.2}{100} = 2.79P\); then proceed as above.

criteria.description: Correct interest expression in terms of P with n = 30
acceptedAlternatives: Equivalent principal 465P for one month or 38.75P for one year

criteria.partialCreditRules: Award if the equation is correct in form with an earlier arithmetic slip in the interest.

questions.authorNotes: Uses the standard simple-interest formula for recurring deposits taught in ICSE Class 10. Numbers chosen so that 32.79P = 39348 gives an exact whole-rupee answer.

content.stem: Meera deposits ₹600 per month in a recurring deposit account for 1 year at 9% per annum simple interest. The interest she earns at maturity is:

hints: Each instalment earns interest for a different number of months: 12, 11, 10, … , 1.

commonMistakes: Treating the whole ₹7,200 as if it were deposited for the full year: \(7200 \times \tfrac{9}{100} = ₹648\), option (a).
Not dividing by 12, so the rate is applied per month: ₹4,212, option (d).

questions.authorNotes: Distractors correspond to the three errors listed in commonMistakes.
